nodes.description: Because the DYSF coding sequence exceeds single AAV capacity, two overlapping AAVrh74 vectors sharing a region of homology reconstitute the full-length cDNA. In dysferlin-deficient mice this restored dysferlin expression and membrane repair, and it was well tolerated in non-human primates. A phase I intramuscular trial (NCT02710500) has completed; no efficacy result is cited here.

evidence.reference_title: AAV.Dysferlin Overlap Vectors Restore Function in Dysferlinopathy Animal Models.
evidence.snippet: The two vector system (AAV.DYSF.DV) packages the dysferlin cDNA utilizing AAV serotype rh.74 through the use of two discrete vectors defined by a 1 kb region of homology.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic Delivery of Dysferlin Overlap Vectors Provides Long-Term Gene Expression and Functional Improvement for Dysferlinopathy.
evidence.snippet: Treated muscles showed a significant decrease in central nucleation, collagen deposition, and improvement of membrane repair to wild-type levels.

evidence.reference_title: Phase I Intramuscular Gene Transfer Clinical Trial for Dysferlin Deficiency Delivering the Dysferlin Gene by AAVrh74
evidence.snippet: The proposed clinical trial is a double-blind, randomized controlled study with direct intramuscular injection of rAAVrh.74.MHCK7.DYSF.DV gene vector to the extensor digitorum brevis muscle (EDB).

nodes.description: Weakness of the anterior compartment of the legs, the first sign in DMAT.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlinopathy.
evidence.snippet: DMAT is characterized by early and predominant distal muscle weakness, particularly of the muscles of the anterior compartment of the legs.

nodes.description: After injury, dysferlin-deficient muscle shows delayed clearance of necrotic fibers, a prolonged inflammatory phase and delayed functional recovery, with reduced early neutrophil recruitment and reduced cytokine release from myoblasts; satellite cell activation and myoblast fusion appear normal. Patient biopsies contain an excess of immature fibers.

evidence.reference_title: Attenuated muscle regeneration is a key factor in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Satellite cell activation and myoblast fusion appear normal, but there is a reduction in early neutrophil recruitment in regenerating and also needle wounded muscle in dysferlin-deficient mice.

evidence.reference_title: Attenuated muscle regeneration is a key factor in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Primary mouse dysferlinopathy myoblast cultures show reduced cytokine release upon stimulation, indicating that the secretion of chemotactic molecules is impaired.

evidence.reference_title: Attenuated muscle regeneration is a key factor in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We have observed that dysferlinopathy patient biopsies show an excess of immature fibres and therefore investigated the role of dysferlin in muscle regeneration.

nodes.description: Truncating, splice, missense and copy-number DYSF variants on both alleles leave dysferlin absent or markedly reduced in muscle (and in blood monocytes). Neither variant class nor residual protein level explains the clinical variability in the natural history cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Calcium-sensitive phospholipid binding properties of normal and mutant ferlin C2 domains.
evidence.snippet: We found that C2A, the first C2 domain of dysferlin and myoferlin, bound 50% phosphatidylserine and that phospholipid binding was regulated by calcium concentration. A dysferlin point mutation responsible for muscular dystrophy was engineered into the dysferlin C2A domain and demonstrated reduced calcium-sensitive phospholipid binding.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlin, a novel skeletal muscle gene, is mutated in Miyoshi myopathy and limb girdle muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We describe nine mutations in the dysferlin gene in nine families; five are predicted to prevent dysferlin expression.

evidence.reference_title: DYSF mutation analysis in a group of Chinese patients with dysferlinopathy.
evidence.snippet: Eight patients showed an absence or drastic decrease of dysferlin expression in biopsied muscle.

evidence.reference_title: The Clinical Outcome Study for dysferlinopathy: An international multicenter study.
evidence.snippet: There is a high degree of variability in disease onset, pattern of weakness, and rate of progression. No factor, such as mutation class, protein expression, or age at onset, accounted for this variability.

nodes.description: Weakness of the gastrocnemius and soleus, spreading proximally over years.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlinopathy.
evidence.snippet: MMD (median age of onset 19 years) is characterized by muscle weakness and atrophy, most marked in the distal parts of the legs, especially the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.

evidence.reference_title: Miyoshi myopathy and limb girdle muscular dystrophy R2 are the same disease.
evidence.snippet: There is a continuum of distal involvement at any given degree of proximal involvement and patients do not fall into discrete distally or proximally affected groups.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlin, a novel skeletal muscle gene, is mutated in Miyoshi myopathy and limb girdle muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We describe nine mutations in the dysferlin gene in nine families; five are predicted to prevent dysferlin expression. Identical mutations in the dysferlin gene can produce more than one myopathy phenotype (MM, limb girdle dystrophy, distal myopathy with anterior tibial onset).

evidence.reference_title: A gene related to Caenorhabditis elegans spermatogenesis factor fer-1 is mutated in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2B.
evidence.snippet: Using a positional cloning approach, we have identified the gene for a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy that we previously mapped to chromosome 2p13 (LGMD2B).

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlinopathy in the Jews of the Caucasus: a frequent mutation in the dysferlin gene.
evidence.snippet: Three ethnic clusters have previously been described in Dysferlinopathy: the Libyan Jewish population originating in the area of Tripoli, Italian and Spanish populations.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, molecular, and protein correlations in a large sample of genetically diagnosed Italian limb girdle muscular dystrophy patients.
evidence.snippet: Truncating mutations determined earlier onset than missense substitutions (20+/-5.1 years vs. 36.7+/-11.1 years; P=0.0037).

nodes.description: In normal muscle, dysferlin-enriched membrane patches form at sarcolemmal injuries and fibers reseal in the presence of calcium; dysferlin is trafficked to the injury site with MG53 (TRIM72) and caveolin-3. In dysferlin-null fibers, vesicles accumulate beneath the sarcolemma and the calcium-dependent resealing fails, while the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex remains intact.

animal_models.description: Laser-wounded dysferlin-null fibers fail to reseal in the presence of calcium.
animal_models.name: Dysf-null mouse (targeted knockout)

evidence.reference_title: Defective membrane repair in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, dysferlin-deficient muscle fibres are defective in Ca2+-dependent sarcolemma resealing.

evidence.reference_title: Defective membrane repair in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that dysferlin-null mice maintain a functional dystrophin-glycoprotein complex but nevertheless develop a progressive muscular dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Membrane repair defects in muscular dystrophy are linked to altered interaction between MG53, caveolin-3, and dysferlin.
evidence.snippet: MG53 mediates active trafficking of intracellular vesicles to the sarcolemma and is required for movement of dysferlin to sites of cell injury during repair patch formation.

nodes.description: Calf (gastrocnemius and soleus) or tibialis anterior atrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Attenuated muscle regeneration is a key factor in dysferlin-deficient muscular dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlinopathy.

nodes.description: Lower limb muscle fat fraction on MRI increases with age and earlier onset; muscles acting on the same joint movement progress together.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling of Dysferlinopathy (LGMDR2) Progression: A Longitudinal Fat Fraction Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Muscles that participated in the same joint movement progressed similarly over time. FF was expected to be higher the older patients were and the earlier the age at symptom onset.

nodes.description: Lost muscle is replaced by adipocytes derived from fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs). In dysferlin-deficient mice, annexin A2 accumulating in the myofiber matrix drives FAP adipogenesis; deleting annexin A2 or pharmacologically inhibiting FAP adipogenesis protected muscle. In patients, MRI fat fraction rises with age and with earlier symptom onset.

evidence.reference_title: Fibroadipogenic progenitors are responsible for muscle loss in limb girdle muscular dystrophy 2B.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that FAPs cause the adipogenic loss of dysferlin deficient muscle. Progressive accumulation of Annexin A2 (AnxA2) in the myofiber matrix causes FAP differentiation into adipocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Lipid accumulation in dysferlin-deficient muscles.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling of Dysferlinopathy (LGMDR2) Progression: A Longitudinal Fat Fraction Analysis.

nodes.description: Dysferlin is enriched in the transverse-tubule membrane and can tubulate membranes. Under membrane stress, dysferlin-deficient fibers show structural and functional t-tubule disruption that is reduced by lowering external calcium or blocking L-type calcium channels with diltiazem, and diltiazem reduced eccentric contraction-induced damage, inflammation and necrosis in dysferlin-deficient mice.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlin stabilizes stress-induced Ca2+ signaling in the transverse tubule membrane.
evidence.snippet: dysferlin-deficient muscle fibers undergo extensive functional and structural disruption of the t-tubules that is ameliorated by reducing external ... or blocking L-type Ca(2+) channels with diltiazem.

evidence.reference_title: Dysferlin mediates membrane tubulation and links T-tubule biogenesis to muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Dysferlin tubulates liposomes, generates a T-tubule-like membrane system in non-muscle cells, and links the recruitment of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate to the biogenesis of the T-tubule system. Pathogenic mutant forms interfere with all of these functions
